questions.question: A scalable enterprise network is one that:

options.B: Handles more users, devices and traffic without losing performance

questions.explanation: A scalable network handles more users, devices and traffic without losing performance.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the 3 objectives (H-S-S) of a scalable enterprise network?
questions.explanation: The three objectives are High Availability, Security and Scalability; low bandwidth is not an objective.

questions.question: Which layer of the hierarchical design is the main backbone?
questions.explanation: The Core layer is the main backbone of the hierarchical design.

questions.question: Which layer connects user devices like PCs, printers and phones?
questions.explanation: The Access layer connects user devices such as PCs, printers and phones.

questions.question: Dividing a network into small parts like HR, Finance and IT is called:
questions.explanation: Dividing a network into separate small parts such as HR, Finance and IT is modular design.

questions.question: Load balancing means:

options.D: Spreading traffic across many paths or devices

questions.explanation: Load balancing spreads traffic across many paths or devices.

questions.question: POVualizing the campus WAN design creates:

options.A: Many POVual networks on one shared physical network
options.B: One POVual network on many physical networks

questions.explanation: Network POVualization creates many POVual networks on one shared physical network.

questions.question: A VLAN splits one physical network into groups at which layer?
questions.explanation: A VLAN works at Layer 2 (the data link layer).

questions.question: Border nodes in a fabric:

options.C: Connect the fabric to outside networks

questions.explanation: Border nodes connect the fabric to outside networks.

questions.question: Edge nodes in a fabric:

options.A: Let user traffic enter the fabric

questions.explanation: Edge nodes let user traffic enter the fabric.

questions.question: A WAN is used to connect:

options.D: LANs across cities, states or countries

questions.explanation: A WAN connects LANs across cities, states or countries.

questions.question: MPLS forwards data using:
questions.explanation: MPLS (Multiprotocol Label Switching) forwards data using labels.

questions.question: The Customer Edge (CE) router is:

options.B: A type of switch in the core

questions.explanation: The CE router is the gateway of each branch.

questions.question: SD-WAN means:
questions.explanation: SD-WAN is software-defined control of the WAN.

questions.question: VPLS connects distant LANs so that they work:
questions.explanation: VPLS connects distant LANs so that they work like one LAN.

questions.question: The control plane:
questions.explanation: The control plane decides where traffic goes.

questions.question: The forwarding plane:
questions.explanation: The forwarding plane actually sends the traffic.

questions.question: VRF stands for:
questions.explanation: VRF stands for POVual Routing and Forwarding.

questions.question: The RIB (Routing Information Base) stores:
questions.explanation: The RIB stores routes.

questions.question: The FIB (Forwarding Information Base) is used to:
questions.explanation: The FIB is used to forward packets.

questions.question: A POVual Network (VN) is:
questions.explanation: A POVual Network is a group of interconnected VRFs.

questions.question: 802.1Q adds what to an Ethernet frame?
questions.explanation: 802.1Q adds a tag to the Ethernet frame.

questions.question: The 802.1Q tag contains the:
questions.explanation: The 802.1Q tag contains the VLAN ID.

questions.question: GRE was developed by:
questions.explanation: GRE (Generic Routing Encapsulation) was developed by Cisco.

questions.question: Does GRE provide encryption by itself?
questions.explanation: GRE does not provide encryption by itself.

questions.question: L2TP creates the tunnel but:
questions.explanation: L2TP only creates the tunnel and gives no encryption by itself.

questions.question: IPsec gives:
questions.explanation: IPsec provides encryption and security.

questions.question: Simple meaning: L2TP = tunnel, IPsec = ?
questions.explanation: L2TP is the tunnel and IPsec is the lock, because it secures the traffic.

questions.question: PPTP uses how many bits for keys (as per notes)?
questions.explanation: As per the notes, PPTP uses 128-bit keys.

questions.question: L2TP uses how many bits for keys (as per notes)?
questions.explanation: As per the notes, L2TP uses 256-bit keys.

questions.question: L2TPv3 can carry:

options.A: Ethernet frames and more Layer 2 protocols

questions.explanation: L2TPv3 can carry Ethernet frames and other Layer 2 protocols.

questions.question: In dynamic routing, the routing table:
questions.explanation: In dynamic routing, the routing table updates automatically.

questions.question: In static routing, routes are entered:
questions.explanation: In static routing, routes are entered manually by the administrator.

questions.question: EIGRP and RIP are examples of which routing protocol type?
questions.explanation: EIGRP and RIP are Distance Vector protocols.

questions.question: BGP stands for:
questions.explanation: BGP stands for Border Gateway Protocol.

questions.question: VRRP stands for:
questions.explanation: VRRP stands for POVual Router Redundancy Protocol.

questions.question: Topology-Aware Routing (TAR) keeps traffic:

options.D: In the zone where it started

questions.explanation: TAR keeps traffic in the zone where it started.

questions.question: TAR is mainly discussed in which platform?
questions.explanation: Topology-Aware Routing is mainly discussed in Kubernetes.

questions.question: Multi-Topology Routing (MTR) lets you configure:

options.A: Different forwarding topologies for different traffic types

questions.explanation: MTR lets you configure different forwarding topologies for different traffic types.

questions.question: Which traffic types are given as examples for MTR?
questions.explanation: Voice, video and data are the example traffic types for MTR.

questions.question: Which is a problem of large Layer 2 domains?
questions.explanation: Large Layer 2 domains suffer from loops and increased broadcast traffic.

questions.question: Is an end-to-end VLAN desirable for large networks?

options.C: No, it creates a big Layer 2 domain

questions.explanation: An end-to-end VLAN creates a big Layer 2 domain, so it is not desirable for large networks.

questions.question: A POVual Firewall (VFW) filters traffic between:
questions.explanation: A POVual Firewall filters traffic between POVual machines.

questions.question: SDN splits a switch into:
questions.explanation: SDN splits a switch into a control plane and a data plane.

questions.question: NFV runs network functions:
questions.explanation: NFV (Network Functions POVualization) runs network functions in software.

questions.question: OTV (Overlay Transport POVualization) extends:
questions.explanation: OTV extends Layer 2 connectivity across locations.

questions.question: A single-hop data path example is:
questions.explanation: An Ethernet link using 802.1Q VLAN tags is a single-hop data path.

questions.question: A multiple-hop data path example is:
questions.explanation: An IP cloud using GRE tunnels spans multiple hops.

questions.question: The Fabric in campus POVualization is:

options.B: A shared pool of network resources used to build VNs

questions.explanation: The Fabric is a shared pool of network resources used to build POVual Networks.

questions.question: Services POVualization means:

options.A: Each group has its own DNS
options.D: Different groups share services like DNS and security

questions.explanation: Services POVualization lets different groups share services such as DNS and security.

questions.question: A company grows from 50 to 500 employees and the same network supports them without being rebuilt. Which objective is this?
questions.explanation: A network that supports growth without being rebuilt achieves scalability.

questions.question: If one link fails and another link keeps services running, the objective achieved is:
questions.explanation: Services continuing after a link failure is High Availability.

questions.question: A sale website automatically gets more resources when visitors rise from 1,000 to 10,000. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Automatically gaining resources as demand rises is an example of cloud-based services.

questions.question: Which layer connects the access layer to the core and manages traffic?
questions.explanation: The Distribution layer connects the access layer to the core and manages traffic.

questions.question: Why are VTEPs used in a campus fabric?
questions.explanation: VTEPs (VXLAN Tunnel Endpoints) handle VXLAN traffic in the campus fabric.

questions.question: Where does the physical-to-logical mapping happen?
questions.explanation: The physical-to-logical mapping happens in Edge Control.

questions.question: Transport POVualization is used to:

options.C: Carry many POVual networks over one physical network

questions.explanation: Transport POVualization carries many POVual networks over one physical network.

questions.question: Which WAN technique is reliable, secure and good for strict SLAs?
questions.explanation: MPLS is reliable and secure and suits strict SLAs.

questions.question: WAN POVualization can combine which links into one POVual network?
questions.explanation: WAN POVualization can combine MPLS, broadband and cellular links into one POVual network.

questions.question: Automatic failover (a backup path if one fails) is a benefit under:
questions.explanation: Automatic failover is a performance and reliability benefit.

questions.question: Offices in Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru connected together form a:
questions.explanation: Offices in different cities connected together form a WAN.

questions.question: Which is the correct flow in WAN architecture?

options.D: ISP → MPLS Cloud → CE Router → Branch LAN → Devices

questions.explanation: The flow is ISP → MPLS Cloud → CE Router → Branch LAN → Devices.

questions.question: Device POVualization POVualizes:
questions.explanation: Device POVualization POVualizes processes, databases, tables and interfaces inside a device.

questions.question: "Each VN has its own forwarding table" is a property of the:
questions.explanation: As per the key, a separate forwarding table for each VN is a property of the forwarding plane.

questions.question: Keeping Layer 2 domains small:
questions.explanation: Small Layer 2 domains improve scalability.

questions.question: Which is a reason large Layer 2 domains are a problem?
questions.explanation: In large Layer 2 domains Spanning Tree becomes complex.

questions.question: As per the notes, VLANs should be used only between:
questions.explanation: VLANs should be used only between the access and distribution layers.

questions.question: In campus networks, a VLAN ends at the routed core and then:

options.B: Maps to a segment in the core

questions.explanation: A VLAN ends at the routed core and maps to a segment there.

questions.question: Control-plane-based POVualization means:

options.C: Restricting routing information so each VN has only its own subnets

questions.explanation: Control-plane-based POVualization restricts routing information so each VN has only its own subnets.

questions.question: Which method of connecting VRFs is costly and inefficient?
questions.explanation: Using dedicated physical links to connect VRFs is costly and inefficient.

questions.question: Multiple-hop data-path POVualization over IP is done by:
questions.explanation: Multiple-hop data-path POVualization over IP is done by tunnelling.

questions.question: Each VLAN has its own:

options.B: MAC table and Spanning Tree instance

questions.explanation: Each VLAN has its own MAC table and Spanning Tree instance.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.A: VRF is like VLAN but at Layer 3
options.D: VRF and VLAN are the same thing

questions.explanation: VRF is like a VLAN but works at Layer 3.

questions.question: Network POVualization uses:

options.C: A network hypervisor and controller software

questions.explanation: Network POVualization uses a network hypervisor and controller software.

questions.question: At the GRE receiver, the headers are:
questions.explanation: The receiver removes the headers in reverse order.

questions.question: Limitations of GRE include:

options.D: No encryption and difficulty in scaling

questions.explanation: GRE has no encryption and is difficult to scale.

questions.question: In L2TP + IPsec, "authenticated twice" means:
questions.explanation: Authenticating twice makes it more secure but slower.

questions.question: Which is slightly faster and easier to set up?
questions.explanation: PPTP is slightly faster and easier to set up.

questions.question: L2TPv2 can carry only:
questions.explanation: L2TPv2 can carry only PPP frames.

questions.question: Which statement about L2TPv3 is true?

options.C: It works only inside one LAN
options.D: It can carry IPv6 over IPv4

questions.explanation: L2TPv3 can carry IPv6 over IPv4.

questions.question: The Best Path Selection Algorithm is used by:
questions.explanation: BGP uses the Best Path Selection Algorithm.

questions.question: VRF allows:

options.C: Multiple routing tables in one router

questions.explanation: VRF allows multiple routing tables in one router.

questions.question: VRF is often used with:
questions.explanation: VRF is often used with MPLS VPNs.

questions.question: TAR works best when:

options.D: Traffic is evenly distributed and there are 3 or more endpoints per zone

questions.explanation: TAR works best when traffic is evenly distributed and each zone has 3 or more endpoints.

questions.question: In TAR, a request from Zone A goes to:
questions.explanation: In TAR, a request from Zone A goes to an endpoint in Zone A.

questions.question: A main benefit of TAR is:
questions.explanation: TAR reduces cross-zone cost and latency.

questions.question: MTR supports which protocols/routes (as per notes)?
questions.explanation: As per the notes, MTR supports OSPFv2, static routes and BGP.

questions.question: Class-based forwarding in MTR is used to:
questions.explanation: Class-based forwarding in MTR is used to differentiate services.

questions.question: Which statement correctly separates TAR from MTR?

options.A: MTR routes by traffic type; TAR routes by zone/location
options.B: TAR routes by traffic type; MTR routes by zone

questions.explanation: MTR routes by traffic type, while TAR routes by zone or location.

questions.question: Metro Ethernet providers use 802.1Q as a:
questions.explanation: Metro Ethernet providers use 802.1Q as a Layer 2 VPN.

questions.question: Besides the VLAN ID, the 802.1Q tag also has a:
questions.explanation: The 802.1Q tag also has a priority field.

questions.question: In GRE, the GRE packet is wrapped inside:
questions.explanation: The GRE packet is wrapped inside an IP packet, the transport protocol.

questions.question: Which tunnelling protocol, developed by Cisco, makes a POVual point-to-point tunnel?
questions.explanation: GRE, developed by Cisco, makes a POVual point-to-point tunnel.

questions.question: Two VMs on the same server, and a VFW decides if they may talk. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: A VFW deciding whether two VMs may talk is POVual Firewall filtering of VM-to-VM traffic.

questions.question: In SDN, the data plane:
questions.explanation: In SDN, the data plane moves the frames.

questions.question: In the 3-layer hierarchical design, printers and PCs connect at the:
questions.explanation: Printers and PCs connect at the Access layer.

questions.question: Which memory point is correct?

options.A: Edge = entry, Border = exit to outside

questions.explanation: Edge nodes are the entry into the fabric, and Border nodes are the exit to outside networks.

questions.question: "Control everything from one central interface" is the benefit of:
questions.explanation: Controlling everything from one central interface is the Simplified management benefit.

questions.question: The first step in implementing WAN POVualization is:
questions.explanation: The first step is assessing the existing network.

questions.question: Why use a routed infrastructure for large networks?

options.D: To avoid the problems of large Layer 2 domains

questions.explanation: A routed infrastructure avoids the problems of large Layer 2 domains.

questions.question: Which statement about GRE is TRUE?

options.A: It encrypts all data by default
options.B: It builds a point-to-point tunnel but adds no encryption
options.D: It can carry only IP traffic

questions.explanation: GRE builds a point-to-point tunnel but adds no encryption.

questions.question: An ISP offers an L2TP VPN, but the customer needs the data to be confidential. What should be added?
questions.explanation: L2TP gives no encryption by itself, so IPsec should be added for confidentiality.

questions.question: Why is load balancing limited in large Layer 2 domains?
questions.explanation: Loop prevention (Spanning Tree) blocks redundant links, which limits load balancing.

questions.question: Which pair is correctly matched?

options.C: SDN – splits control plane (software) and data plane

questions.explanation: SDN splits the control plane (software) from the data plane; the other pairs are wrong.

questions.question: Two customers share one physical router, and each needs a separate routing table and forwarding table. Which feature is used?
questions.explanation: VRF gives each customer a separate routing table and forwarding table on one router.

questions.question: Which is NOT a part of a VRF instance?
questions.explanation: A VRF instance consists of a RIB, a FIB and interfaces; the 802.1Q priority field is not part of it.

questions.question: Which statement about the control plane is INCORRECT?

options.A: It maintains topology and avoids loops
options.B: It physically sends the traffic out of the interface
options.C: It uses protocols, databases and tables
options.D: Each VN has its own topology view in it

questions.explanation: Physically sending traffic is the job of the forwarding plane, so this statement is incorrect.

questions.question: "Each POVual Network has its own topology view" refers to the:
questions.explanation: Having its own topology view is a property of the control plane.

questions.question: Which statement correctly separates Edge nodes from Border nodes?

options.A: Edge nodes connect to outside networks; Border nodes let users in
options.B: Both only connect to outside networks
options.C: Edge nodes let user traffic enter the fabric; Border nodes connect the fabric to outside networks

questions.explanation: Edge nodes let user traffic enter the fabric, while Border nodes connect the fabric to outside networks.

questions.question: Which statement about PPTP vs L2TP is INCORRECT?

options.D: PPTP uses 256-bit keys and is more secure than L2TP

questions.explanation: PPTP uses 128-bit keys and is less secure than L2TP, so this statement is incorrect.

questions.question: Because L2TP over IPsec authenticates data twice, the result is:

options.A: More security but slightly slower speed

questions.explanation: Double authentication gives more security but slightly slower speed.

questions.question: Which is the main improvement of L2TPv3 over L2TPv2?

options.C: It carries Ethernet frames and other Layer 2 protocols across an IP backbone
options.D: It works only inside one LAN

questions.explanation: L2TPv3 can carry Ethernet frames and other Layer 2 protocols across an IP backbone.

questions.question: Which is NOT a listed feature of MTR?

options.D: Support for OSPFv2, static routes and BGP

questions.explanation: Built-in encryption of all traffic is not a listed MTR feature.

questions.question: Why does MTR create separate topologies for voice, video and data?

options.D: So each traffic type can have its own forwarding path

questions.explanation: Separate topologies let each traffic type have its own forwarding path.

questions.question: TAR may NOT work well if:

options.A: Incoming traffic is unevenly distributed or a zone has too few endpoints
options.C: Each zone has 3 or more endpoints

questions.explanation: TAR may not work well when traffic is uneven or a zone has too few endpoints.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.A: TAR separates voice from video traffic
options.B: TAR routes by location/zone; MTR routes by traffic type
options.C: MTR keeps traffic inside a Kubernetes zone
options.D: TAR and MTR are the same

questions.explanation: TAR routes by location or zone, while MTR routes by traffic type.

questions.question: Which feature mainly aims to reduce cross-zone cost?
questions.explanation: TAR mainly aims to reduce cross-zone cost.

questions.question: Which is the correct function of the Distribution layer?

options.D: Connects access to core and manages traffic

questions.explanation: The Distribution layer connects the access layer to the core and manages traffic.

questions.question: A Wi-Fi network grows from 200 students to 1,000 during an event and still works well. Which techniques help?
questions.explanation: Load balancing and SDN help the network scale to many more users.

questions.question: Dividing a network into HR, Finance and IT sections for easier management and growth is:
questions.explanation: Dividing a network into sections such as HR, Finance and IT is modular design.

questions.question: What is the relationship between Fabric and POVual Networks?

options.A: VNs are used to build the fabric
options.B: Fabric is a type of VLAN tag
options.C: Fabric is the shared pool of resources used to build VNs

questions.explanation: The Fabric is the shared pool of resources used to build the VNs.

questions.question: Which pair is correct?

options.B: Services POVualization – carrying VNs over cables
options.D: Services POVualization – groups share DNS and security services

questions.explanation: Services POVualization lets groups share services such as DNS and security.

questions.question: In a campus network, a VLAN in the wiring closet acts as:

options.A: The entry point into a VN

questions.explanation: A VLAN in the wiring closet acts as the entry point into a VN.

questions.question: Why does a VLAN end at the routed core and map to a segment there?

options.B: To avoid an end-to-end Layer 2 domain

questions.explanation: Ending the VLAN at the routed core avoids an end-to-end Layer 2 domain.

questions.question: An end-to-end VPN across switched and routed parts of a campus is formed by:

options.C: Mapping VLANs to segments in the routed core

questions.explanation: Mapping VLANs to segments in the routed core forms an end-to-end VPN.

questions.question: Why are dedicated physical links per VN a poor choice for connecting VRFs?
questions.explanation: Dedicated physical links per VN are costly and inefficient.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the 4 components of WAN architecture in the notes?
questions.explanation: VTEPs belong to the campus fabric, not to the WAN architecture components.

questions.question: The MPLS cloud is best described as:

options.A: A packet-switching network that uses labels to forward data between branches

questions.explanation: The MPLS cloud is a packet-switching network that uses labels to forward data between branches.

questions.question: Which WAN POVualization benefit is shown by "giving priority to cloud traffic"?
questions.explanation: Giving priority to cloud traffic is the Cloud connectivity benefit.

questions.question: Which feature is a key strength of SD-WAN compared with plain MPLS?

options.C: Dynamic path selection with software control

questions.explanation: SD-WAN offers dynamic path selection with software control.

questions.question: A POVual bridge that makes distant LANs behave like one LAN describes:
questions.explanation: VPLS acts as a POVual bridge that makes distant LANs behave like one LAN.

questions.question: Which technique can combine MPLS, broadband and cellular into one POVual network?
questions.explanation: WAN POVualization can combine MPLS, broadband and cellular links into one POVual network.

questions.question: In GRE, what is the order of events?

options.A: Receiver encrypts; sender decrypts; packet is dropped
options.B: Packet is dropped; GRE is removed; IP is added
options.C: Payload is wrapped in GRE, then in IP; receiver removes headers in reverse order
options.D: IP is removed first; GRE is added later

questions.explanation: The payload is wrapped in GRE and then in IP, and the receiver removes the headers in reverse order.

questions.question: What does "transparently" mean for 802.1Q across a provider network?

options.A: The provider can read all customer data
options.B: Customer traffic crosses the provider network without being changed by it

questions.explanation: Transparently means customer traffic crosses the provider network without being changed by it.

questions.question: Which is a Layer 2 protocol used to carry VLAN traffic between switches?
questions.explanation: 802.1Q is the Layer 2 protocol used to carry VLAN traffic between switches.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about device POVualization and data-path POVualization?

options.B: Data-path POVualization creates logical devices inside a box
options.C: Data-path POVualization POVualizes the connection between devices
options.D: Device POVualization POVualizes only the links

questions.explanation: Data-path POVualization POVualizes the connection between devices, while device POVualization creates logical devices inside a box.

questions.question: Which statement about dynamic vs static routing is WRONG?

options.B: Static routes are entered by the administrator
options.C: Dynamic routing adapts to route changes
options.D: Static routing adapts automatically to route changes

questions.explanation: Static routing does not adapt automatically to route changes, so this statement is wrong.

questions.question: BGP is classified as which type of routing protocol?
questions.explanation: BGP is a Path Vector routing protocol.

questions.question: Which pair of protocols belong to the Distance Vector type?
questions.explanation: EIGRP and RIP are Distance Vector protocols.

questions.question: Which protocol automatically assigns an available IP router to hosts?
questions.explanation: VRRP automatically assigns an available IP router to hosts.

questions.question: VRF on routers is most similar to which concept on switches?
questions.explanation: VRF on routers is similar to VLANs on switches.

questions.question: VRF combined with MPLS is useful because it:

options.A: Can create separate VPNs for different customers

questions.explanation: VRF with MPLS can create separate VPNs for different customers.

questions.question: A POVual Firewall is most useful for:

options.B: Inspecting and blocking unapproved traffic between VMs

questions.explanation: A POVual Firewall inspects and blocks unapproved traffic between VMs.

questions.question: Network POVualization moves networks from static to:
questions.explanation: Network POVualization makes networks dynamic, agile and optimized.

questions.question: Which is a role of VLANs in scalability?

options.D: Reduce the size of the broadcast domain

questions.explanation: VLANs help scalability by reducing the size of the broadcast domain.

questions.question: L2TP was originally described as an extension of:
questions.explanation: L2TP was originally described as an extension of PPTP.

questions.question: Which is a GRE limitation (as per notes)?

options.B: It needs other security protocols like IPsec for protection

questions.explanation: GRE needs other security protocols such as IPsec for protection.

questions.question: For TAR to work well, each zone should have at least how many endpoints?
questions.explanation: Each zone should have at least 3 endpoints.

questions.question: Which statement best describes MTR's multicast handling?

options.B: Multicast uses the unicast topology only
options.D: A separate multicast topology can be used

questions.explanation: MTR can use a separate multicast topology.

questions.question: A college's Computer Science, Management and Administration departments share the same cables and switches but each has its own POVual network. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Departments with separate POVual networks on shared cables and switches are an example of campus WAN POVualization.
